units.spec_id: F-176 / foundations.md §7 installers (Windows NSIS/MSI, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm)
units.deviation: M4 packaging is an open decision: foundations.md:187-190 and :278 plan NSIS/MSI plus AppImage/deb/rpm built from CI, but ADR 0003 §8 and features.md:283 mark the old PyInstaller/Inno/AppImage build F-176 Drop and decision-sheet.md:12 substitutes the Tauri bundler; docs/todo.md:169 records the unresolved clash over what M4 even contains. The repo has a bundler config and a manual workflow, not a shipped installer.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\inno\modrinth_bulk_downloader.iss:9-30 (Inno Setup [Setup] with AppId, OutputBaseFilename ModrinthBulkDownloader_Setup_{#MyAppVersion}, localappdata install dir, x64-only) and D:\latest_project\packaging\linux_appimage\README.md:18-39 (APPIMAGETOOL build producing a 0.14.0rc1 AppImage plus .sha256). New side: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-37 sets bundle.active=true and targets="all" with icon entries, but no built installer is checked in; .github/workflows/bundle.yml:3-4 is workflow_dispatch only, and :31-36 runs `pnpm tauri build` then uploads target/release/bundle/**. The documented replacement is the Tauri bundler, so absence of the old EXE/AppImage artifacts is the recorded F-176 decision, not a silent regression.

units.deviation: foundations.md:187 asks for code signing to reduce SmartScreen warnings and :278 assigns it to M4, while docs/todo.md:169 records M4's definition as an unresolved user decision. The old Windows binary was never signed either, so this is a planned-but-not-yet-delivered release step, not a regression.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\pyinstaller\ModrinthBulkDownloader.spec:102-119: the GUI EXE(...) sets codesign_identity=None, entitlements_file=None, console=False — no Authenticode step; the diagnostics EXE at :124-141 likewise sets codesign_identity=None. The only signing in the old tree is license-payload signing (packaging/license/create_offline_license.py:80-97, Ed25519), which ADR 0003 §1 drops with F-175. New side: .github/workflows/bundle.yml:22-31 installs toolchains and runs pnpm tauri build with no signing or notarization step, and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-37 has no signing identity. Signing material must not live in source (AGENTS.md §5.11), so its absence here is expected.

units.deviation: foundations.md:189,278 specify tauri-plugin-updater with private update-signing keys in M4, and docs/todo.md:169 records the M4 scope conflict. Neither the old app nor the new one self-updates: the old flow is a manual release ZIP/installer and the new crate list has no updater plugin.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\README.md:143-173: releases are produced by build_windows_release.ps1 into artifacts/portable and artifacts/installer with 0.12.x filenames, and README_WINDOWS_RELEASE.md:7-15 uses the root `build.ps1 windows-public` wrapper — a manual distribution path with no in-app updater. New side: src-tauri/Cargo.toml:16-33 lists tauri, tauri-plugin-opener, tauri-plugin-dialog, serde, ts-rs and mm-core; there is no tauri-plugin-updater dependency. .github/workflows/bundle.yml:33-36 only uploads the bundle as a CI artifact rather than publishing an update feed or release.

units.deviation: The old app silently kept using ~/.modrinth_bulk_downloader when its database existed. ADR 0003 §3 replaces that with an explicit M4 button reading an old home into new instances with a backup first (F-181 Keep/later), and docs/todo.md:169 records the M4-scope conflict. The new repo implements the explicit path, so the loss of silent migration is deliberate and documented.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\app\config.py:68-90: _resolve_roots documents 'keep using the legacy root so existing users do not appear to lose data' and :86-90 returns LEGACY_APP_DIR roots when legacy_db exists and platform_db does not — an automatic, no-prompt relocation of user data. New side: src-tauri/src/commands/legacy.rs:1-8 states the scan never opens the old home for writing; :50-57 scan_legacy_import is a read-only report, :59-75 plan_legacy_import writes nothing, :77-89 execute_legacy_import re-scans, rebuilds the plan in Rust and registers folders after backing up our own database. docs/todo.md:18 records that actual registration ran under commit 636c332 with installed_mods import deferred per ADR 0006 §7.

units.deviation: Old release engineering had an explicit rc freeze and promotion gate (0.14.0rc1 -> 0.14.0). foundations.md:190 expects tauri-action builds on every release and :278 puts distribution in M4, while ADR 0003 §8 keeps only a small set outside v1 and docs/todo.md:169 records M4's contested content; no release channel exists in the new repo yet.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\run_phase16_19_36_rc_freeze_preflight.py:10-12 (EXPECTED_VERSION = "0.14.0rc1"), :46-60 (writes a phase16.19.36 RC-freeze report with pass/fail counts) and :70-80 (checks a signoff template carrying the marker 'Promote `0.14.0rc1` to `0.14.0`'). New side: Cargo.toml:5-6 declares one workspace version 0.1.0 with no prerelease suffix and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:4 repeats 0.1.0; .github/workflows/bundle.yml:3-4 is manual workflow_dispatch with no v-tag trigger and no promotion or release job.

units.deviation: Old release process produced a measured bundle-size audit; the new workspace has size-oriented Cargo profiles but no size measurement artifact. foundations.md:40 sets the smaller-WebView2-installer goal and §15 demands measured baselines, while docs/todo.md:169 leaves M4 distribution open — the missing measurement belongs to the open release work, not to an undocumented deviation.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\analyze_bundle_size.ps1:34-43 (Get-TreeSize walks dist/ModrinthBulkDownloader), :51-60 (initializes the report and emits bundle_total, _internal, PySide6, plugins and qml sizes), with packaging/README.md:235-243 documenting the Phase 12.4 cut from full PySide6 to PySide6-Essentials. New side: Cargo.toml:9-12 sets debug='line-tables-only' because E: is a slow HDD, and :18-22 sets release codegen-units=1, lto=true, opt-level=3, panic='abort', strip=true while citing the Tauri size guide — that is a build policy, but no size report or installer baseline exists anywhere in the repo.

units.spec_id: F-178 packaged diagnostics / F-150-F-151 in-app diagnostics
units.deviation: features.md:285 marks F-178 (self-diagnostics plus build templates) Drop with the reason 'يستحق فقط مع الترخيص', yet the new app ships a different, in-app diagnostics surface (F-150/F-151): sanitized startup reports and app-path inspection over IPC. The standalone console helper has no equivalent binary; that is the recorded Drop plus the M4 conflict at docs/todo.md:169, not a silent loss of diagnostics.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\diagnostics_entry.py:13-20: main() calls app.diagnostics.handle_cli_args(), and app/diagnostics.py:55-70 provides runtime_paths_lines() and self_check_lines() backing --paths/--self-check; packaging/README.md:103-120 documents ModrinthBulkDownloaderDiagnostics.exe with --diagnostics-report and --packaged-qa. New side: src/lib/ipc.ts:481-498 exposes appPaths() and openAppFolder(kind) for the data/config/cache/logs roots, src-tauri/src/lib.rs:50-76 writes a sanitized startup_failure.txt report before any window exists, and src/app/pages/SettingsPage.tsx:43 renders the diagnostics group. The user-visible diagnostics survive the migration; the extra console EXE does not.

units.deviation: Old releases wrote release_manifest_<version>.json, a text summary and SHA-256 checksums with required-artifact and ZIP-content checks. The new bundler workflow uploads raw artifacts only; release manifests, signing and distribution are M4 work whose definition is still open (foundations.md:190,278 vs ADR 0003 §3; docs/todo.md:169).
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\packaging\generate_release_manifest.ps1:14-19 (resolves artifacts/reports), :21-45 (Get-AppVersion reads the diagnostics exe --paths or falls back to app\config.py) and :62-80 (Test-ZipContents checks entry counts and required GUI/diagnostics/_internal members); packaging/README.md:260-281 lists release_manifest_0.12.5.json, release_summary_0.12.5.txt and checksums_sha256_0.12.5.txt. New side: .github/workflows/bundle.yml:31-36 runs pnpm tauri build and uploads target/release/bundle/** with no checksum, manifest or signoff step between the build and the upload.

units.spec_id: core Rust crates (tokio / reqwest / rusqlite / zip / ts-rs)
units.evidence: Crates.io API read 2026-11-24 for the exact pins: tokio 1.53.3 (core/Cargo.toml:29) published 2026-10-13, license MIT, not yanked, crate last updated 2026-10-21 with max 1.54.1; reqwest 0.13.5 (:21) published 2026-09-08, license MIT OR Apache-2.0, crate updated 2026-09-08, max 0.13.5; rusqlite 0.40.2 (:22) published 2026-08-08, license MIT, crate updated 2026-11-15 with max 0.43.0; zip 9.0.4 (:36) published 2026-10-16, license MIT, crate updated 2026-11-23 with max 9.8.2. ts-rs 12.0.1 is pinned at src-tauri/Cargo.toml:21, published 2026-01-31, license MIT, last release then with 11.7M recent downloads. Old requirements.txt:1-3 held only PySide6-Essentials>=6.6.0, requests>=2.31.0 and cryptography>=42,<47 — lower bounds, no hashes. The five pins cover async runtime, HTTPS+rustls, SQLite, ZIP and generated IPC types with permissive licenses and 67M-326M recent downloads; rusqlite and zip trail registry maxima, which is a freshness observation, not a behavioral deviation.

units.spec_id: frontend npm packages (React / Tauri API / Tailwind CSS)
units.evidence: npm registry read 2026-11-24: react pinned ^19.1.0 at package.json:33 (19.1.0 published 2025-03-28, license MIT) while latest is 19.3.1 published 2026-10-14; tailwindcss pinned ^4.3.3 at :36 (4.3.3 published 2026-07-16, license MIT) while latest is 4.3.5 published 2026-11-06; @tauri-apps/api ^2 at :24 resolves to 2.12.5 published 2026-11-16, license Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Registry 'modified' timestamps are 2026-11-23 for react and tailwindcss, showing active maintenance. The old UI runtime dependency was PySide6-Essentials>=6.6.0 (requirements.txt:1), a Qt binding; foundations.md §3.3 and ADR 0001 replace it with React 19 + Tauri 2 + Tailwind 4. Every new npm license above is permissive, so no copyleft UI framework survives the rewrite.

units.deviation: The project license itself is still an open decision (foundations.md:306 'اسم المشروع والرخصة | تُحسم قبل النشر'), and ADR 0003 §1 drops the old proprietary activation stack outright. src-tauri/Cargo.toml:7 therefore declares license = "" rather than inventing one; this is the documented open item, not an undocumented omission.
units.evidence: Old runtime license obligations from requirements.txt:1-3: PySide6-Essentials (LGPLv3/commercial dual), requests (Apache-2.0) and cryptography (Apache-2.0 OR BSD), plus the 16-stage offline activation layer in app/licensing.py that F-175 and ADR 0003 §1 remove. Registry check 2026-11-24 of every pinned new dependency: tokio MIT, reqwest MIT OR Apache-2.0, rusqlite MIT, zip MIT, ts-rs MIT, react MIT, tailwindcss MIT, @tauri-apps/api Apache-2.0 OR MIT — all permissive, no copyleft obligation carried over. In the new repo src-tauri/Cargo.toml:7 is literally `license = ""` and no LICENSE file exists at HEAD; foundations.md:306 leaves the project name and license to be settled before publication, and docs/todo.md:169 keeps release work open with M4.

Crates.io API maintenance data read 2026-11-24 for the exact pins: tokio 1.53.3 published 2026-10-13 with the crate updated 2026-10-21 and 326M recent downloads; reqwest 0.13.5 published 2026-09-08 with 282M recent; rusqlite 0.40.2 published 2026-08-08 while the crate itself was updated 2026-11-15 (67M recent); zip 9.0.4 published 2026-10-16 with the crate updated 2026-11-23 (111M recent); ts-rs 12.0.1 published 2026-01-31, license MIT, 11.7M recent downloads and no newer release — the slowest-moving of the five but still current. npm side: react 19.3.1 published 2026-10-14, tailwindcss 4.3.5 published 2026-11-06, @tauri-apps/api 2.12.5 published 2026-11-16. Old requirements.txt:1-3 pinned only lower bounds (>=6.6.0, >=2.31.0, >=42,<47) and recorded no maintenance metadata; the new pins are exact and their release/update dates are recorded here.

units.deviation: The old application exposed no mod-management command line: app/diagnostics.py:60-70 only implements a packaging self-check. foundations.md §4.1 and :275 make the CLI a thin client of core and part of the M1 exit criterion, so the new eight-command surface is a documented addition, not a missing old feature.
units.evidence: Read D:\latest_project\app\diagnostics.py:55-70: runtime_paths_lines() and self_check_lines() are the entire old command-line surface, dispatched by packaging/diagnostics_entry.py:16-20. New cli/src/main.rs:32-103 defines eight clap subcommands — Info, Search, Scan, List, Plan, Install, Update, Remove — with --game/--loader on the read ones and --yes/--dry-run on Install (:69-70), Update (:90-92) and Remove (:100-102). cli/src/commands/install.rs:27-48 resolves slugs through core's Provider, prints the plan and only then builds the Downloader. cli/src/main.rs:6-7 states the CLI is a thin client of mm-core where every mutation is plan-first, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:100-105 actually exercises `cargo run -p mm-cli -- install sodium lithium ... --yes` as the M1 gate.

Old side: D:\latest_project\app\ui\main_window.py:7194-7214 is a Qt slot import_installed_scan_matches_to_profile that calls self.profile_controller.begin_installed_import(profile.id, present_project_ids, ...) directly from the window — domain work reached inside the UI process. New side: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-190 enumerates the typed command surface (search_projects, build_install_plan, scan_instance, preview_toggle/execute_toggle, legacy scan/plan/execute at :159-161, pack plan/execute at :165-174, backup, target and watch), while :1-9 keeps state, providers, progress and dto as the only Tauri modules. AGENTS.md §5.1-5.2 require core to have no UI dependency and the webview to reach files only through commands; src/lib/ipc.ts:98-785 is the sole caller, and every mutation is split into a read-only preview command and a separate execute command.

units.spec_id: F-072 typed IpcError codes and i18n translation
units.evidence: Old side: D:\latest_project\app\services\mrpack_installer.py:168-173 defines MrpackInstallError and MrpackInstallCancelled as typed Python exceptions, and features.md:129 records the old installer's 26 named error codes as the model for IpcError { code }. New side: src-tauri/src/dto.rs:56-127 is a 24-variant ErrorCode enum with semantic codes (packChanged, linkOrReparse, newerSchema, restoreMismatch, backupChanged, notOurExport, updateContextChanged, updateBackupNotConfirmed); :132-140 defines IpcError { code, message, retry_after_seconds? }, :149-158 derives error.<camelCase> from the serialized serde name so the key cannot drift, and :178 discards provider response bodies. src/i18n/en.json:61-85 carries 25 translated error.* strings (the extra error.startupDetailUnavailable is used only by the native dialog at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:66). The webview normalizes any rejection at src/lib/ipc.ts:779-785 and renders t(`error.${code}`) at src/app/pages/BrowsePage.tsx:515 — typed code, localized message, no raw string.

Old side: D:\latest_project\app\services\batch_install_plan.py:40-53 defines frozen BatchInstallPlan(summary, entries, warnings) with requires_confirmation() true for more than one item, dependencies, blocked entries, warnings or a backup-overwrite — a preview gate before any write; profile_content_toggle.py:56-73 likewise separates build_content_toggle_preview from execute_content_toggle_preview. New side: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:127-190 registers the same shape as pairs — plan_create_instance/execute_create_instance (:140-141), preview_toggle/execute_toggle (:135-136), preview_remove_content/execute_remove_content (:137-138), plan_modpack_install/execute_modpack_install (:165-166), plan_instance_restore/execute_instance_restore (:178-179), preview_update_install/execute_update_install (:183-184). src/lib/ipc.ts:545-552 records that the apply re-reads the archive and rebuilds the plan in Rust, so the on-screen plan is never sent back as truth, and src-tauri/src/commands/legacy.rs:25-30 repeats that rule for legacy import.

Old side: D:\latest_project\app\services\profile_content_toggle.py:56-70 build_content_toggle_preview validates the action, builds a ContentTogglePlan and returns it without renaming anything; :73-100 is the separate execute that performs the guarded renames. New side: cli/src/main.rs:69-70, :90-92 and :100-102 expose --dry-run on Install, Update and Remove; cli/src/commands/install.rs:29-32 prints the resolved plan and returns Ok(()) before confirmation, download or lock write; cli/src/commands/plan.rs:1-17 is the pure read-only preview (`Never writes`). On the GUI path the same contract is the preview_* commands in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:135,137,178,183, for example src-tauri/src/commands/legacy.rs:59-75 where plan_legacy_import writes nothing. AGENTS.md §5.4 'plan first, execute second' is therefore enforced in both clients.

units.spec_id: F-020 progress streaming via Tauri Channels
units.evidence: Old side: D:\latest_project\app\services\download_manager.py:24-27 declares ProgressCallback(title, downloaded, total), StateCallback plus Pause/Cancel callbacks, called per 256 KiB chunk at :110-134 with the pause/cancel loop at :111-128. New side: src-tauri/src/progress.rs:13-46 defines MIN_INTERVAL_MS=100 and ProgressThrottle, which emits the first event and then at most one per 100 ms but always passes terminal events; :54-96 maps core ItemProgress onto i18n-key phases, and :122-150 keeps pack DONE/FAILED/WRITTEN/SKIPPED decisive so no row is left stuck. The webview constructs a real Channel at src/lib/ipc.ts:359-377 (verifying the __CHANNEL__:<id> wire form) and hands it to executeInstall at :389-398. Tests spec_f005_throttle_sends_the_first_event_and_then_holds and spec_f020_the_terminal_batch_event_is_a_field_not_an_inference pin the 100 ms floor and terminal pass-through. Same information as the old callbacks, now ordered and throttled per AGENTS.md §5.7.
